cells.date: Śāka 1313, Prajāpati, Caitra ba. 5, Tuesday, solar eclipse=1391 A.D., April 4, f.d.t. 23. But the eclipse occurred on the next day.
cells.remarks: Records the creation of the agrahāra called Mañchālāpura by combining the two villages Cōvalli and Mauli and the tulā-puruṣa-hōma land (bhū-dāna) to the tank called Māli-chali-samudra by Mādhava-daṇḍanāyaka, son of Bācha-baṭṭa, gōtra, son of Chandighaṭṭa and Māchāmbikhā. Also records the grant of the agrahāra to 12 Rigvēdi Brāhmaṇas of various gōtras, belonging to different villages. It is also stated that a piece of land near the stone on the eastern side, probably of the above village, was named as Mādhavapura. Written in Sanskrit, in Telugu characters of the same period refers in general terms to the former gifts of villages made by the kings of the Kadamba dynasty and other rulers.

cells.place:
TIRUNELVĒLI DISTRICT
• Tirunelvēli.—Plates secured through Shri K. Padmanabhan, I.A.S., District Revenue Officer, Tirunelveli.
cells.remarks: Records the grant, by the king, of the village Paļļakkāl in Muļi-nādu in Tiruvadi-rājya for meeting the personal expenses of pūjā, lamps and offerings to the deity Vēńkațēś-vara at the temple at the cost of the chieftain Krishnappa, son of Kōnēribhūpāla and grandson of Obalayya, who was a disciple of Parānkuśa-muni. It is stated that this chief, who was the ruler of the Tiruvadi (Tiruvadi)-rājya and a devotee of the deity at the temple, built the mukhamandapa, gōpura,etc. for the temple and that he approached the king for securing the grant of the village as directed by the god himself in the dream.

cells.remarks: Original charter issued from Kāñchīpura. the present century.ingly a later copy in characters of the 7th century A.D. Records the grant of the village Udayāndiram as a brahmadēya and aranya land in Adevāra-rāshțra to a brahmadēya to Kuļar-charman (Kuļasarman), a resident of Kāñchīvāyil, who belonged to the Kauśika-gōtra, Pravachana-sūtra and Taittirīya-charaņa. There is an endorsement in Tamil dated in the 22nd year of (Nandivarman) and in the reign of Perunandichōla I recording the clubbing together of Kāñchīvāyil alias Igannamangalam and Udayachandramangalam into one village. Published in Ep. Ind., Vol. III, pp. 142 ff. and Plate.

cells.remarks: The chief seems to claim his descent from the lunar race and his three brothers, Gaṅga, Kēsava and [Siddhi] are mentioned. States that when Kauṇdēva-Mahārāja, the Vaidumba chief, was ruling over Aṇdāpurppalaṭṭaṇam, Mahāmaṇḍalē-śvara Allugangai-Chōla-Mahārāja and [Uchcha]ppa-mahā-kāmanta alias Rāyarapuram to Perumāl Sōmayāji-bhaṭṭar of Kōmappuram, for the merit of Rāyadeva who is stated to be the maternal uncle (amāmama) of the donor. The village was divided into 36 parts and distributed amongst a number of Brāhmaṇas of different gōtras and sūtras. In characters of the 13th century A.D.

cells.remarks: States that Rēvaṇa took the oath in the presence of the representatives of the twelve liṅgas, the sixteen of the eight groups, and five-hundred of Ayyāvoḷe to kill Saṁmanāka who had killed Mañgaja and that he fulfilled the same by entering the village when Saṁmanāka was eating and drinking the blood of the murderer. In the course of this vendetta he is also stated to have killed twelve persons including two babies in the cradle. An assembly of the above mentioned bodies gave Rēvaṇa the title 'poyeya- beṇkoḷva' and exempted him from the payment of certain taxes. Published in Karnataka Inscriptions, Vol. IV, pp. 119 ff.

cells.date: Śaka 1452, Vikāri, Āshāḍha śu. 3, Sunday=1530 A.D., May 20.
cells.remarks: Records the gift of bhūmi of land in Sūrapuram situated in Singavarasa Kallūru in Ghunḍikōṭa-rājya by god Chennakeśava to Ayyappa, son of Singayya-Seṭṭi, son of Sūrisimhi of Kūśayapa-gōtra. The gift was made for the merit of the king on the occasion of a lunar eclipse. The land seems to have known been entrusted to the care of Bhūgam Chennayya and Pūnayya, who were themselves the recipients of mānyam portions of land for their own maintenance. Cf. Nos. 1, 3 and 5 above.

In characters of about the 14th century.

cells.location: NALGONDA DISTRICT SURYAPET TALUK Pillalamarri — Telangana
cells.place: Four-faced pillar set up on a platform in the compound of the Śiva temple. First face.
cells.date: Śaka 1117 (śuila-tārāpati-bhava), Rākshasa, Vai-śākha śu. 5, (Kusumāsāra-tithi), Sunday=1195 A.D., April 16, f.d.t. 12.
cells.remarks: States that Bēcheruvula Nāmirēḍḍi, son of Kāma, had three lingas, Kāmēśvara, Kāchēśvara and Nāmēśvara, installed at trikūṭa in Pillalamarri after the names of his parents and after his own name for their merit as Sahasralinga-pratishṭhā. A gift of land was made to the Śivālayam besides 7 martūru of dry land for worship and offerings to the deities. Also records a gift of land near Viśvanāthasamudram to god Nāmēśvara and further lands under Kuḍukuḍiya-Gaura-samudram for the maintenance of the gardens of the temple. Published in Hyderabad Archaeological Series, No. 13, Inscription No. 38.

cells.remarks: Gives the genealogy of the Rēcherla family to which Nāma (Nāmi-reḍḍi) belonged and states that he had filled the god Viśvanāthēśvara temple with ornaments, gift of the two tanks called Guṇḍacheruvu and Kaṭavācheruvu and lands under them as vritti; Aitami, wife of Nāma and Viśvanātha, their son, installed the deities Aitēśvara and Viśvanāthēśvara respectively and made endowments of lands for the same. cells.remarks: States that Erapāṁbā, wife of Pillalamarri Bēti-reddi of the Recherla family had the deity Erakkēśvara (named after her) installed in the village Pillalamarri and endowed lands under the tank Erakasamudra, which she had bought, constructed by her in the village Pillalamarri, for worship, offerings, repairs,etc. in the temple and for maintaining the members of the establishment and the maṭha attached to it; further gifts of land were made to the same temple by Erapāṁbā and her husband Kāmasēvāra and Erakkēśvara installed by her and named after her parents; also records grants for a temple (?) constructed by her brother Nūṁka-nāyaka. The genealogical accounts of both Erapāṁbā and her husband Bēti-reddi are given in the beginning. Ibid., no. 42.

cells.date: Śaka 1137, Yuva, Māgha ba. 15, Friday, solar eclipse= 1218 A.D., February 19.
cells.remarks: Engraved in continuation of the above. Further gifts of lands to the deities Erakēśvaradēva and Mūlasthāna-Māchidēva set up on the tank-bund of Erakasamudra, and to the deities Bētēśvara and Erakkēśvara installed by Imaturī Sōmayya, are registered. cells.location: Ghōshārvā, Patna District, Bihar. — Bihar
cells.place: Stone slabs in the same Museum. First Pāla slab.
cells.remarks: Records the construction of a building for the Vajrāsana by Vīradēva who hailed from Nagarāhāra and who was the son of the Brāhmaṇa Indragupta. He is also stated to have studied two Vedas by the time he was nine. Gives a detailed account of his deep study of the Vedas, his becoming a Buddhist monk ultimately heading the Nālanda monastery, his visit to the Kanishka-vihāra and Vājrasana and his influence over the king Dēvapāla. In characters of about the 10th century. Published in JASB, Vol. XVII, pl. I, pp. 492-501; Ind. Ant., Vol. XVII, pp. 307-312; and Gauḍalēkha-mālā, pp. 45-54 and Plate.

cells.location: Deōpāḍā, Rajshahi District, East Pakistan.
cells.place: Slabs in the Indian Museum.
cells.remarks: Records the building of a temple of Pradyumnēśvara by the king whose genealogy and eulogy are given. The king is said to have defeated Nānya, Vīra and the kings of Gauḍa, Kāmarūpa and Kaliṅga, imprisoned Rāgha, Vardhana and Vīra; led a naval expedition along the course of the Ganges. The composer and the engraver of the inscription were Umāpatidhara and Rāṇaka Śūlapāṇi respectively. Published in JASB, Vol. XXXIV, Pt. 1, pp. 128-54; Ep. Ind., Vol. I, pp. 305-15 and Plate; and Inscriptions of Bengal, Vol. III, pp. 42-56 and Plate.

cells.place: A third slab in the same place
cells.date:
(1) Śaka 1347, Krōdhi, Āshāḍha śu. 1.
(2) Śaka 1354, Paridhāvi [?], Bhādrapada [?] ha. 7, Wednesday. Irregular.
(3) Śaka 1355, Paridhāvi, Kārttika śu. ...
cells.remarks: States that Hariyāṇa-sūri (or Harihara-sūri), pupil of Siṁhanandyāchārya, who was himself a pupil of Vidyāṇandasvāmi, died on the second date and that the memorial slab (niśidhi) was set up by him. Records the gifts of the village Vāgaṇāḍu and Akshaya made on the first and the third dates respectively to the Nēminātha-basti at Bandavaḍa. The gifts were entrusted to Muniyanna, pupil of Siṁhanandyāchārya and were to be administered by his sons and grandsons. It is stated that at the time, Sōma, son of Laṇdā, was governing Gōvē. An endorsement at the end of the record states that the place Bandavādi was established by a king named Śrīpāla in early days and Virugapa, son of Maṁgadaṇḍa, built the temple of Nēminīrtha, and that the latter was renovated at the instance of Simhanandi.

cells.remarks: Records the renovation of the temple by Maṇḍalāchārya Vijayakīrtti, the gurubhātā of Dēvēndrabhūshaṇa, during the time of Pārichhēta-Mahārāja-Bhāshāha. cells.location: Rānōd
cells.place: Eastern niche of Akhti Bāōḍī. Impressions from the Superintendent, Archaeological Survey of India, Nag- pur. (Acc. Nos. 2176 and 1840).
cells.language: Bilingual. Local dialect, Nāgarī; Persian, Masta līq.
cells.remarks: Records the construction of the bāōḍī (i.e., step- well) by Bhavyā Sīradāsa and bhavyā Śītaladāsa and some others. Seems to refer to other connected constructions by nine others, described as residents. Mentions Bēḍī in sūbā Sahijahānābād, probably as the native village of the donors. For the Persian portion, see A. R. Ep., 1961-62, App. D. No. 75, which is dated one month earlier.

Records a royal order issued from the seat Mañavārāyan, at the instance of [Malai]yāvarāyan as king's kambam, directing that a piece of land, purchased as kuḻamāi, antarāyam etc., payable on various pieces of land, bought of Tiruk-kōdikā-uḍaiyān Tirukkadambanārdiṇ alias Kongarāyan of Pūmbijāl in Kāfai-irukkai, the kīrāṇ of Variviyūr and various others and gifted as the maintenance (jīvitam) of the services engaged to be performed in the temple for god Tiruvalāvāyu-ḍaiyān-nāyaṇār of Madurai in Mādakkulakkīl, instituted by Oruvāṇar-āṇḍiṇ Enakku-nalla-Porumāl alias Aṇṇan Tamil-la-pPallavaraiyar of Rājavallabhapuram in Kil-Vemba-nāḍu. In continuation of this record, a copy and the vāśakam of the same transaction, both being dated on the 479th day of the same year, are engraved.

cells.remarks: Records the gift of 132 sheep for two perpetual lamps to god Tirumarai-nāyanār. One of the lamps was gifted by a certain Senthālaiarai Protkalan-Uḍaiyān of Tiruvadavūr in Ten-parappu-nāḍu and the other by Maṇikkanār. Both these lots of sheep were entrusted in equal lots to three cowherds (surabhi-dāyin) of the temple who agreed to supply ghee for the lamps.

cells.location: Tiruvādāvūr—contd. / Melur taluk—contd. †
cells.place: Same wall
cells.date: Year 30, Makara śu. 13, Saturday, Hasta. Irregular.
cells.remarks: Do. Seems to record a sale of land in the dēvadāna Kāṇamangalam alias Māhēśvaranallūr to provide for the burning of a lamp in the temple of god [Phaṇīdharēśvara]. It is stated that the land had lain fallow due to the silting up of the tank and refers to the non-payment of the poṉvari. As a consequence, Śrīvallabha Vilupparaiyar is mentioned in this connection. Rājagōpāla is also mentioned. Cf. Nos. 485, 493 and 494 above.

cells.remarks: Do. Contains the king's praśasti, Pāṇimalai Tiruvivum etc., and appears to record the king's order issued at the instance of Malavarāyan probably giving the taxes on the lands given to the deity, amounting to 120 ekas as a new endowment to offerings to god Chēnnārāyana-viṇnagarālvar set up at Chēnnārāyana-maṅgalam by Nārāyaṇa-bhaṭṭan in the name of his father Śrīrāma-bhaṭṭan mentioned above. cells.date: Śaka 1303, Durmati, Tai 6, ba. 1, Wednesday = day of Pushya 6, 1382 A. D., January 1.
cells.remarks: Records a regrant made by an assembly of the peoples from for several agaram and villages as well as the bhaṭṭas from far off places mentioning that in respect of the marriage of Uḍaiyār and Gāṅgēyarāyar, that in the marriages among the members of the Brāhmaṇa community, the bridegroom should pay only 8 kaḻañju each of gold and silver, and not more, for the jewels of the bride, and that the transgressors of the above regulation would be deemed to have lost their caste.

cells.location: Tiruvāymūr
cells.place: Tiers of the same wall
cells.remarks: Records a gift of 50 kāśu paid into two temple treasury by Pañchāṇvaraiyaṉ to maintain two perpetual lamps, one each before god Tiruvāymūr-uḍaiyār for the merit of Vēlān-bhaṭṭan alias Iśānavirāyaṉ and the other before the goddess in the temple for the merit of the donor's fore- fathers. The perunguri-sabhā of Iśanūr alias Paramēśvara- chaturvēdimagalam in Āla-nādu having received the money made the temple land included in the same tax-free that the lease-holders of the said land should contribute ghes towards the maintenance of the lamps.

cells.place:
Tyāgarājasvāmi temple, Tiruvāyūr.—south
nētha shrine. Tiers of the west wall.
cells.remarks: Records the gift of a brass lamp with nūrādam (rōd) and 600 kāśu for maintaining the same by Vīramindān alias Paramēśvaran ... dēvan of Pampūṟr-uḍaiyān Tirunīrruvvaman- udaiyan, a merchant residing at Piśai, stipulating that the lamp may be burnt during the three sandhis. The Sivabrāh- maṇas of the temple received the amount and agreed to maintain the endowment.

cells.place:
Idaiyāttumaṅgalam.—Maṅgalyēśvara
temple, central shrine, north, west and
south walls.
cells.remarks: In fragments. Seems to record an undertaking given by the peruṅguḍi-sabhā of Tiṇvaṅkāvīl to remit for a specific period (?) the tax on some lands purchased by Rājarāja- brahmārayar from the kuḍimakkaḷ of the place and granted as dēvadāna by him, in lieu of 150 kalañju of gold which the sabhā owed the nadu. The ruler of the land is referred to in the body of the record. Mentions Dataṇ Ūlāyabhūṣaṇa and others of the Rākṣatāra-gōtra who owned lands bounding the land granted. Cf. No. 634 below. In characters of about the 11th century.

cells.location: Kottamangalam.—contd. †
cells.place: Central shrine, north wall
cells.remarks: Commences with the prasasti, Tirumaḍagal pōla etc. Records an endowment given by one Śōraiyan Sōraiyan of Rājakēsari-Vishṇugriham to celebrate a festival on the day of Sadayam every month, and another festival in the month of Chittirai to extend over seven days ending on the day of Sadayam, the natal star of the king, with 300 kaļam of paddy produced out of the produce of a piece of land formerly granted as dēvadāna to the god but which was not being utilised, on the orders of Avanam-uḍaiyān Māttāṇḍan, a panimagan of the king who checked the accounts of the temple in the course of his 'inspection' in the nādu during that year. Mentions the measure Rājakēsari-marakkāl.

Tirukkuḷūr.—Vaiḷatanāthasvāmipuṟuṇal
temple. Central shrine. North wall.
cells.remarks: Commences with the praśasti, Pāṇṇular-iḷaiyar, etc., of the king. Records the king's order from his seat Maṇīcarājan in his palace at Madurai, issued at the request of Aiyan Malavarāyar to the ūrār of Tirukkuḷūr and Pīraiguṛuṅkudi remitting the taxes and dues payable by them with the measuring poles in the villages after having measured them with the measuring pole of 18 feet named Vīraṇḍāyilvḛḻ-kōl as the same lands remained untilled due to the excessive taxes levied previously. The measure of capacity called Muḍal-Vīraṇḍaiyan is also mentioned. Cf. No. 521 above.

cells.location: TIRUNELVELI DISTRICT / TIRUCHENDUR TALUK †
cells.place: West wall of the same shrine
cells.remarks: Commences with the king's prasasti, Pi maṛavaiya Tiruma- valarntaruli, etc. Records an order of the king from the seat Maḷavarāyam, issued at the request of Malavarāyan, grant- ing the village Vallakkulam in Ammaduṇa-valanādu exclud- ing the lands given as kārāṇmai to Śrīmaṇan Periyanambi alian Kulaśēkhara-Brahmarājan of Nallur, as a tax-free paṇḍāravāḍai on 100 paṇams for maintaining a 4 Thul kōlil in Tiruvuḍai-valanādu, for conducting a festival in the temple in the month of Paṅguni, the festival terminating with āṛātu on the day of Avittam, the natal asterism of the king. The gift took effect from the 20 + 10 year of the king. Cf. Conchology in the Cholas of the royal order. Text published in Sentamil, Vol. XII, pp. 346 ff.; Prakusti alone published in South India and Her Muhammadan Invaders, pp. 208 ff.

cells.location: Raṅjōle-Klēgī
cells.place: Slab kept behind the Hanumān temple.
cells.remarks: Broken into three pieces and badly worn out. Registers gifts of lands and money to gods Hemmēsvara and Mallikārjuna of Reṇjēru by mahamaṇḍalēśvara Bhairavadeva of the Sinda family whose genealogical account is given in detail. The gift was made into the hands of Varēvaradeva who was the sthānapati of the temple of Farēśvara and a disciple by the mahājanas and other individuals to the deity Hemmēsvara, and to the Brāhmaṇas of the Brahmapurī of that god and also to Bhāskara who wrote the record are enumerated. Reṇjēru is said to have been situated in Aṭṭale-nāḍu and givas also a genealogy with him of his four sons of Nidulūḍi-Sinda, the progenitor of the family. The other three sons, viz., Satyasārya, Prabhusēvya and Budhasēvya, are stated to have been ruling over Paliyāṁda-maṇḍala, Bigadage-dēśa and Balljāre-nāḍu respectively.

cells.location: Raṅjōle-Klēgī †
cells.place: Slab built into the right wall (outside) of the Hanuman temple.
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land, gardens and income from taxes to god Brahmēsvara of Reṇjēru for worship, offerings and repairs and feeding ascetics etc., after laying the feet of (bhaṭṭāraka) thāru-munīndra for merit of his parents. The priest of Chanrō-pāsīya Barmadēva-daṇḍanāyaka who received the lands from mahamaṇḍalēśvara Bāchidēvarasa of the Sinda family. The record contains genealogical accounts of both these chiefs as also of the co-optor who was the āchārya of the Hōgēs-vara temple. The temple of Brahmeśvara was established by Bāchidēvarasa.

cells.location: Harsūr
cells.place: Three fragments lying near the Parvatadēva temple.
cells.date: Year 42, Hēma-lambi, Paushya śu. 8, Monday, Uttarāyaṇa-saṁkrānti. Vyatīpāta = 1117 A.D., December 3. There was no samkrānti on that day.
cells.remarks: Contains the genealogy of the king and that of Sāgara-sēṭṭi and Bhāskara-sēṭṭi. Records the construction of the temple of god Bālēśvara by Bhāskara-sēṭṭi and of a temple of god Kēdāreśvara by (his brother) Sāvana-sēṭṭi. Also mentions Jagadēkamalla's subordinate Bammanayya, his wife Lakkhādēvi and their son Hemmādēvara. Records the renovation of the temple of god Bālēśvara, originally built by Bāli-sēṭṭi, by Bhāskara-sēṭṭi and the completion of the temple of Kēdāreśvara and another temple by Kēṭi-sēṭṭi, by Sāgara-sēṭṭi in the sarvamānzeya-agrahāra Śāleyasīmala, situated in Gonka-nādu, a sub-division of Ālande-1000 in Kuntala-janapada. Further records that Gorikarasa, the ruler of Gonka-nādu, Nagayya, the prabhu of the village, purahitans and vaidyas Kēṭi-sēṭṭi-together granted 2 māṇa of flower-garden to the deity Bālēśvara for worship in and repairs to the temple, etc. The record enjoins Bammanayya, Lakkhidēvi and Hemmāḍi-dēvarasa, among others, to protect the grant.

cells.place: Chittorgarh.—Broken slab. Impressions from the Superintendent, Archaeological Survey of India, Western Circle, Baroda.
cells.remarks: Fragmentary. Seems to record the construction of a Jain temple. Gives the genealogical list of a Jain family beginning with Jala, Jaskara, and ending with Bhimasiha in Chittrakūṭa (i.e. Chittorgarh). Mentions Āchārya Surasundarīsūri who was probably worshipped by the Chāhamānas, Paramāras and the Gūrjaras. Contains part of a bandha drawn in the centre of the slab. Composed by Śubhākīrti and engraved by Sūdra. In characters of about the 12th century. Cf. PIRASWC, 1904-05, No. 2202.

cells.location: Eṭāwāh
cells.place: Stone lying in the kāfī of a house near the fort gate. Fort is situated 2 miles from the city. Impressions received from the Superintendent, Northern Circle, Agra.
cells.date: Śaka 1271, (śasānka-citi-akshi-dhara), Tāpas (i.e. Māgha), śu. 3 (Girijāthith), Monday=1350 A.D., January 11.
cells.remarks: The king claims to belong to the line of his paternal uncle Jayachandra of Kanauj. Appears to record that at the instance of the king, his purōhita made preparations for a Chaṇḍīmahāyaga, but had to give up and take away the image of Durgā installed in the fort and hid it in a pit (garṭa) fearing that the Mlechchhas (i.e. Muhammadans) might destroy it. In characters of about the 13th century.

cells.location: MADHYA PRADESH †
cells.place: Pillar of temple No. 40
cells.remarks: Late. Records the excavation of a maṭha and the excavation of a tank and a well by Prabhodhasiva of the Mattamayūra (clan) genealogy of the spiritual heads of which is given. Also states that this ascetic repaired and re-excavated a well which was formerly dug by his preceptor Praśāntasiva. The praśasti was composed by Vāmanasiva and was written by Dāmodara. It was engraved by Nīlakaṇṭha by the command of the sūtradhāra Sūrika. Ibid., pp. 198 ff.

cells.remarks: Records the death in battle of Yaśa of the Luṇḍela family, the father-in-law of Ghaṭiāma who is stated to belong to the Chauhāṇa family and who was a feudatory of the king. The praśasti was composed by Chandrakāra and engraved by Vīra. Ibid., pp. 563 ff. The first part, composed by Śrīnivāsa, son of Śrīrānanda, records that the queen Nōhalā, the wife of Kēyūravarsha, erected a temple of Śiva and donated to it a number of villages. The second part, composed by the Śaiva ascetic Hridayaśiva who placed it in the charge of his disciple Aghoraśiva (I) and Nōhalā, made over the monastery of the holy Vaidyānātha also called Nauhalēśvara to the Śaiva ascetic Hridayaśiva who placed it in the charge of his disciple Aghoraśiva (II). The third part which was composed by the Kāyastha Siruka records the payment of taxes by the traders for the benefit of the monastery. The praśasti is stated to have deserved praise from the famous poet Rājaśēkhara. It was written by Nāi, son of the karaṇika Dhīra and was engraved by Nōṇṇa, son of the Sūtradhāra Saṅgama. Ibid., pp. 204 ff.

cells.location: Mozzamābād
cells.place: Tripolia gate of the Mughal tank. Right side.
cells.remarks: Bilingual. Records the excavation of the tank and construction of its foam-walls and gate by Siv (Shiv) Nāth, son of Paras-nāth, son of Bāl Nāth, during the government of Mahārāja Rām Singh. Also states that the text was inscribed by Mekaṭ Rāi, son of Madan Singh, son of Dayā Dās, of the Kāyastha community, resident of Amber, and resident in the Sahāranpur sarkār, who had come to the place along with Jairāmdās, the 'āmil when the jāgīr was in the possession of Mīr Jalāl-d-Dīn and Mīr Ḥusnu'd-Dīn Jīn. For the Nāgarī portion, see No. 551 of App. B.

cells.location: TONK DISTRICT / NIWAI TAHSIL
cells.place: Niwāī.—Jalandarī-jī-kā-Makān (Temple). To the left of the entrance, in the wall.
cells.remarks: Records a farmān issued by Nawwāb Muḥammad Shāh Khān Bahādur (cf. No. 23 above), stating that the officers, the jāgīrdārs and the inhabitants of the town of Niwāī, the old temple (makān) of Jalandarī Nāth known that in the ādak (rent-free land) of the village of Palā'ī (Palā'ī of the maps) should be respected, as was usually done in the past and that the temple of Nāthji should not be interfered with, in any way. The seal of the Nawwāb quoted in the seal engraved at the top of the slab. The order is signed by Daula Muḥammad Shāh Khān Bahādur Jāmī.
